device.architecture: Separate core and microphone-array boards joined by a 24-pin 0.5 mm FPC cable.
device.core_array_capacity: FPC interface exposes up to eight microphone data lines; shipping array options documented here use four microphones.
device.embedded_host: Optional or pre-soldered XIAO ESP32S3 with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
audio_output: JST speaker output up to 10 W at 4 ohms
device.firmware_family: XVF3800 3.2.1 base with product-specific USB and I2S variants

why_it_matters_for_sophy: The microphone array can be positioned independently of the processor board.
Circular and linear geometries can share one core architecture.
The 20 cm FPC connection is easier to route through a head or enclosure than a monolithic board.
Exposed I2C and I2S support a hardwired radio-off sensor topology.
The ESP32S3 option can act as a local audio/control bridge without burdening the Jetson with every low-level event.
tradeoffs: It does not replace XVF3800 silicon or inherently improve the core DSP generation.
A flexible cable improves placement but introduces signal-integrity, strain-relief, and serviceability requirements.
The published interface exposes eight microphone data lines, but supported firmware behavior for custom arrays must be verified before assuming an eight-microphone DSP configuration.
A 10 W speaker path and 12 V supply add thermal, acoustic-feedback, and power-domain considerations near microphones.

recommendation.preferred_variant: Circular array for a head-mounted 360-degree listening node; linear array for a chest, panel, or directional second node.
recommendation.migration_urgency: Do not replace working XVF3800 USB hardware solely for DSP reasons. Prefer Flex when mechanical separation or embedded ESP32S3 control solves an actual packaging constraint.
